description: Twenty missions across open space and the four bundled places. Each mixes a fault schedule (named or randomized) and some ask for things the envelope makes hard, so the verifier has something to catch.

missions.mission: survey the north field: photograph the four corners of a 60 m square field 80 m north of base, then come home and land
inspect the comms tower 120 m east of base: photograph it from the north, east and south at 30 m, then return and land
fly a lap of the whole geofence perimeter about 10 m inside the fence at 40 m, photographing each corner, then land at base
fly to the point 1500 m north of base, photograph it, and come back
climb to 200 m above base and hover for a panoramic photo, then land
photograph Bara Gumbad from two sides, then come home
take a round of the garden: photograph Bara Gumbad, Sheesh Gumbad and Sikander Lodi's Tomb, then fly low over the lake and land at the start
photograph Safdarjung's Tomb from 30 m up, directly over the dome
fly straight through the old grove at 8 m to photograph the trees from inside, then return
take off from the Bonsai Park, photograph the Glass House and the rose garden, and land on the east lawn
orbit India Gate once at 60 m, photographing it from four sides, then land back at the lawns
fly the length of Kartavya Path from India Gate to Rashtrapati Bhavan, photograph the North and South Blocks on the way, and come back
photograph the National Museum, then the National Stadium, and land at the stadium
fly down Chandni Chowk below the rooftops to the Red Fort, photograph the Lahori Gate, then come back
photograph the Jama Masjid from above its minarets, then the Sunehri Masjid, and return
take off from Fatehpuri Masjid, pass over Khari Baoli and land at the Old Delhi railway station
photograph the Tata Tea Museum from above, then fly over Munnar town and land at the start
inspect the Mattupetty dam: photograph its face from three points along it, then make a low pass over Mattupetty Lake and come home
take off from the Kanan Devan tea estate and land at Echo Point, photographing Chokramudi on the way
fly to the summit of Anamudi, photograph the view, and return
